body.x: Advanced materials and packaging technology startup CIT (CEO Seung Jeong) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, which opened on January 6 (local time) in Las Vegas, where it unveiled its CuFlat Package Core (CuFlat-PKGCore).

Last year, CIT exhibited its transparent antenna “Dolphin,” featuring ultra-thin copper circuitry deposited using its proprietary Atomic Sputtering Epitaxy (ASE) technology, and received a CES Innovation Award.

This year, the company once again won a CES Innovation Award by applying the ASE process to glass substrates for semiconductor packaging with CuFlat-PKGCore, marking two consecutive years of recognition. This achievement indicates that CIT has advanced beyond a materials technology startup to become a company specializing in AI semiconductor packaging technologies, and that its technology has been recognized as a consistent, scalable, and sustainable materials solution.

ASE, which underpins CIT’s consecutive awards, is a process that stacks copper atoms layer by layer on insulating surfaces, bonding the copper and the insulator into a single-crystal structure without adhesives. With the ability to precisely control thickness and surface roughness at the nanometer scale, ASE enables high-quality copper deposition on glass. In this area, conventional technologies have faced stability limitations.
ASE’s innovation has also been recognized in academia. Related research was published in Nature in May 2022 and later featured in Advanced Materials, a leading journal in materials science.

The CuFlat Package Core selected for the CES 2026 Innovation Award applies the ASE process to glass substrates used in semiconductor packaging. Achieving surface roughness below 3 nanometers offers a level of flatness more than 200 times smoother than HVLP4 copper foil, considered one of the flattest materials currently used for AI accelerator package substrates.

body.x: Such an ultra-smooth surface significantly reduces signal scattering and loss during high-frequency transmission. This contributes to stable signal integrity and improved power efficiency in packaging environments for AI accelerators, high-bandwidth memory (HBM), and network chips that handle high-speed, high-frequency signals. According to CIT, the material also enables delicate patterning and high-density routing, allowing engineers greater design flexibility in semiconductor packages.

CuFlat-PKGCore also demonstrates advantages in thermal stability. While conventional copper materials tend to oxidize and degrade in performance at temperatures around 100°C, CuFlat-PKGCore maintains stability without oxidation or delamination even at 250°C. This makes it suitable for high-performance AI accelerator packages, where heat generation is significant and thermal stress can affect reliability.

The technology further differentiates itself in process efficiency and environmental impact. CIT uses 100% recycled copper scrap to produce CuFlat-PKGCore and employs a dry ASE deposition process that eliminates the need for seed layers and chemical mechanical polishing (CMP). As a result, carbon emissions are reduced by 95% compared with conventional processes, and chemical wastewater generation is minimized because electroplating is absent.

With its ultra-flat copper structure on glass substrates, CuFlat-PKGCore is expected to meet the demanding design and process requirements of the AI semiconductor industry, supporting the computational performance and memory bandwidth needed in next-generation devices. Given the versatility of glass substrates across cores, interposers, and other package structures, the technology may also emerge as a standard platform in advanced high-density packaging environments such as 2.5D and 3D packaging.

CIT is currently conducting proof-of-concept (PoC) projects with leading companies in the United States and Japan—including glass substrate and transparent antenna manufacturers and semiconductor equipment firms—to supply products leveraging CuFlat-PKGCore and ASE technology. The company is also pursuing joint development of AI accelerator substrates with major domestic corporations.

As CIT expands its global collaboration network across semiconductor hubs such as Korea, the United States, Japan, and Taiwan, it aims to actively promote its technology’s strengths and potential impact to overseas customers through continued participation in CES 2026.

Seung Jeong, CEO of CIT, said, “With two consecutive CES Innovation Awards, our ASE technology has been recognized globally for its technical maturity and potential value. We expect CES 2026 to open new opportunities for collaboration and market development. By delivering stability, energy efficiency, and environmental sustainability required in the AI semiconductor era, we aim to set a new standard in the global semiconductor packaging market.”
